market_holds: Spot about $3.95-4.04 (sealed 4.04 at 18:14 UTC 2026-11-13), -19.5% over 5 sessions and -35% since $6.13 on 2026-10-09, 2.8% above the 52-week low and -90% from the high, on very thin tape (20-day average 63k shares, about $250k a day; Yahoo daily bars). No usable option chain, so no implied move; the median of seven prior print reactions is 5.98% (max 23.95%), five of seven down (sealed baseline). Consensus is thin and inconsistent: one aggregator shows Q3 EPS -$0.81 and revenue $2.8M, another one analyst at $14M revenue and EPS -$3.73; nobody asked a question on the Q2 call. The line the company set is its own reintroduced guide: Q3 revenue $8-11M, FY2026 revenue $50-55M, FY adjusted EBITDA -$22 to -26M (Q2 release, 2026-08-14). Positioning: Khosla controls about 58% including 7.8M penny warrants and 1.74M new $5.754 warrants issued in the 2026-10-14 LanzaJet recapitalization; short interest about 3.5% of shares, 6 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30, per the sweep row). Market cap about $52M basic, about $85M counting the penny warrants, against roughly $55M of locked-up SGLT H shares and an estimated $35-40M of cash.
view: This is a $50M, Khosla-controlled, cash-burning licensor whose balance sheet is mostly a 33.5M-share stake in Beijing Shougang LanzaTech (HK:2553). That stake was marked at $223.1M on 2026-06-30 (HKD 52.20). SGLT closed HKD 13.26 on 2026-09-30, so Q3 will carry a non-cash fair-value loss of about $165M: a GAAP net loss around $175M, EPS around -$13 against a consensus near -$0.81, and total assets roughly halved. That loss is arithmetic on a public quote, and the stock never valued the stake at $223M in the first place: LNZA's whole market cap was about $80M at the time. When the Q2 report showed the matching gain, the stock moved only +2.1%. I do not expect the mark to drive the window, beyond maybe some pre-market headline noise. The real lines are (1) whether the FY revenue guide of $50-55M holds, and (2) cash and financing. The guide implies Q4 revenue of $18-26M, about twice the run rate. Management tied it to certified-ethanol sales 'beginning in Q4 as certified sales scale'. The ISCC EU certification for the Shoulang plant came through (reported between late September and 2026-10-21; UK DfT recognition reported 2026-10-28), but I found no announced first sale or cargo. So a guide trim is a live risk, and so is a guide held up by one cargo. On cash: $48.9M at June 30 and a guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA of -$9 to -13M put September cash somewhere around $35-40M. The guide implies Q4 EBITDA near breakeven, so the 12-month liquidity statement probably survives, but an ATM or Khosla-backed raise stays an overhang. Against all that, the stock has already fallen 35% in five weeks, mostly on the 2026-10-13/14 recap and warrant dilution and on SGLT sliding from HKD 15.76 to about 12. The last week's -19.5% came on thin volume with no news I could find, in tax-loss season, for a name down 90% on the year. Both sides are real, and neither is clearly unpriced. I lean slightly down because of the base rate of distressed-microcap prints (five of seven down here) and the unconfirmed Q4 ramp, but not enough to act on.

recommendation.reason: The large GAAP loss from the SGLT mark is mechanical and public, and the Q2 gain of the same size moved the stock only 2%. The guide question (a Q4 ramp to $18-26M on certified ethanol, with no first sale announced) leans negative. But the stock is already down 35% into the print on dilution and the SGLT slide, and I cannot show the market has not discounted a trim. No mechanism clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A confirmed first certified-ethanol cargo or offtake booked in Q4 with the FY guide reaffirmed (up), or a FY revenue cut plus a fresh equity raise or going-concern language (down).

self_critique: The case for down is stronger than 45 may suggest. The Q4 hockey stick rests on a product sale nobody has seen, the company withdrew guidance once before in 2025, and a guide cut alongside an ATM or raise in a thin, Khosla-dominated float could easily move it 10-20%. The case for up: the stock already trades at roughly the locked SGLT stake plus cash minus burn after a 35% slide, and a single cargo announcement with the print could squeeze a thin tape. Neither side is backed by evidence the price provably lacks.
approach_notes: P4 helped: it kept me from treating the giant GAAP loss as unpriced news, and the Q2 reaction to the matching gain showed the market ignores the mark. P3's freshest-data search found the certification but no sale. With thin coverage there was no consensus to anchor 'priced', which leaves the judgement close to 50.
